title: Inserting and detaching a binary tree node
summary: Change left-child links to insert or detach an intermediate node P while retaining the entire subtree rooted at 2.
context: Root 1 (n1) initially has left child 2 (n2) and right leaf 3. Node 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. The node P to insert holds 0 and both child links are empty. Three panels show preparation, completed insertion, and completed removal, from left to right.
result: Detaching P restores the original links and makes P unreachable from the root. That does not establish that the object’s memory was freed. The entire original left subtree is still present.

frames.title: Inserting and detaching a binary tree node
frames.explanation: First save the reference to node 2 in n2. In the left panel P is separate from the tree. The middle panel executes n1.left = P and P.left = n2, making the left branch 1→P (0)→2. Node 2 keeps children 4 and 5, while P has no right child. The right panel executes n1.left = n2 to bypass P and restore the original tree. Root 1 keeps right child 3 throughout.

prose.title: Inserting and detaching a binary tree node
prose.summary: Change left-child links to insert or detach an intermediate node P while retaining the entire subtree rooted at 2.
context: Root 1 (n1) initially has left child 2 (n2) and right leaf 3. Node 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. The node P to insert holds 0 and both child links are empty. Three panels show preparation, completed insertion, and completed removal, from left to right.
description: The steps below trace the reference changes in the three panels above.
prose.result: Detaching P restores the original links and makes P unreachable from the root. That does not establish that the object’s memory was freed. The entire original left subtree is still present.

steps.title: Prepare to insert P
steps.explanation: Root 1 (n1) has left child 2 (n2) and right leaf 3. Node 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. P (value 0) is outside the tree with two empty links. Save node 2 in n2 before overwriting n1.left so the original left subtree can be reattached intact.
steps.key_state: Before insertion: Root 1 has left child 2 and right leaf 3; 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. P (0) is still outside the tree.
steps.announcement: Show the initial tree and the separate node P to insert.

steps.title: Insert P into the left link
steps.explanation: Execute n1.left = P, then P.left = n2. Root 1 now has left child P (0) and right leaf 3. P has left child 2 and no right child. Node 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. The reference saved in n2 restores the entire subtree rooted at 2, retaining every original node.
steps.key_state: After insertion, root 1 has P (0) on the left and 3 on the right. P has left child 2 and no right child; 2 has left child 4 and right child 5.
steps.announcement: Two assignments to left links insert P between nodes 1 and 2.

steps.title: Bypass P and reconnect the original subtree
steps.explanation: Execute n1.left = n2 to bypass P and restore the original tree. Root 1 has left child 2 and right leaf 3; 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. P can no longer be reached from the root. Its memory has not necessarily been freed.
steps.key_state: After removal: Root 1 has left child 2 and right leaf 3; 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. P is unreachable from the root.
steps.announcement: Execute n1.left = n2 to bypass P and restore the direct link from the root to node 2.
